stages.title: Advanced grammar
stages.hook: A Russian noun can end in six different ways. How do you decide which ending to use?
explain: Russian has six cases. The nominative (мама) is the subject, the genitive (нет мамы) shows "of" or absence, the dative (дать маме) shows the receiver, the accusative (вижу маму) marks the direct object, the instrumental (с мамой) shows "with" or the tool, and the prepositional (о маме) is used after в, на and о.

The case depends on the role of the word and on the preposition or verb before it. У takes the genitive (у мамы), к takes the dative (к маме), с in the sense of "together with" takes the instrumental. For masculine animate nouns the accusative looks like the genitive: вижу брата but вижу стол.
stages.mnemonic: Six cases are six hats: the word puts on the hat that the sentence asks for.
items: instrumental: to write with a pen
sentences: I am going to my mum.
We are talking about the book.

gq.q: Which case follows the preposition у ("at someone's place")?
Which form is correct for "I see my brother"?
gq.why: A masculine animate object uses the genitive-looking accusative.

panel.q: Why is it Я вижу стол but Я вижу брата?
o: Animate masculine nouns take the genitive form in the accusative
panel.why: Animacy affects the accusative in masculine singular and in plurals.

panel.q: In Мы говорим о книге, why does книга end in -е?
o: The preposition о takes the prepositional case
panel.why: The prepositional case is used with о, в and на.

panel.q: Which sentence has the instrumental of accompaniment?
panel.why: С plus the instrumental means together with.

teach.model: Russian has six cases: nominative, genitive, dative, accusative, instrumental and prepositional. The case depends on the role of the word and on the preposition. For example у takes the genitive and с, meaning with, takes the instrumental.

trip.prompt: Find the table of case endings for мама and read the six forms aloud.

stages.title: Complex sentence patterns
stages.hook: In "the book that I read", the word "that" changes its case in Russian. Which one?
explain: Который agrees with its noun in gender and number, but its case comes from its job inside the relative clause: Книга, которую я читаю (accusative, because I read it); Человек, с которым я говорю (instrumental, because of с).

Other patterns: чтобы after verbs of wanting with a different subject takes the past form: Я хочу, чтобы ты пришёл. The conditional uses бы: Если бы я знал, я бы сказал. Pairs such as не только... но и (not only... but also) and connecting words like как только (as soon as) and несмотря на то, что (despite the fact that) build longer sentences.
stages.mnemonic: Gender from the noun, case from the clause.
items: the book that I am reading
the man who lives next door
the man with whom I speak
If I knew, I would say.
Если бы я знал, я бы сказал.
sentences: If I knew, I would tell you.
The book that I am reading is interesting.

gq.why: Чтобы with a different subject takes the past-tense form.

gq.q: Why is it книга, которую я читаю?
o: Nominative, because книга is the subject
Dative, because the book is given to someone
Которую is accusative: the book is the object of читаю
Genitive, because the book is absent
gq.why: The case of который comes from its role in the clause.

panel.q: Which part of который shows the gender?
panel.why: Gender follows the noun described.

panel.q: What does бы add in Я бы сказал?
panel.why: Бы marks the conditional.

panel.q: Which version is more natural?
o: Как только он придёт, мы начнём
Как только он придёт, мы начинаем всегда
Как только он пришёл, мы начнём всегда
Как только придёт он, мы начали
panel.why: Russian uses the future in both clauses for a future event.

teach.model: Который agrees with its noun in gender and number, but its case comes from its job in its own clause. Use чтобы with a past form when the subjects differ, and бы for conditionals.

points.ask: How do I make a conditional?

trip.prompt: Find relative clauses with который and mark its case in each example.

stages.title: Extended conversations
stages.hook: In a long conversation Russians use small words such as "кстати" and "ну". What do they do?
explain: Extended conversations need connecting words. Кстати (by the way) adds a new topic, на самом деле (actually) corrects an idea, вот именно (exactly) confirms, and ну works as a thinking pause. To disagree gently, say Я не совсем согласен (I do not entirely agree).
Polite requests use the conditional: Не могли бы вы мне помочь? (Could you help me?). Use Как вам сказать... when you look for the right words. Active listening shows interest: Правда? and Понятно.
stages.mnemonic: Кстати opens a side door in the conversation.
items: Не могли бы вы мне помочь?
nye mag-LEE by vy mnye pa-MOCHT
sentences: By the way, have you decided yet?
I do not entirely agree with you.

gq.q: What does Кстати do in a conversation?
o: It introduces a related new point

gq.why: Не совсем is a polite way to disagree.

panel.q: Why use Не могли бы вы...? instead of Помогите?
o: The conditional is more polite and indirect
panel.why: Indirect requests soften the tone.

panel.q: What is the function of ну in speech?
panel.why: Ну is a discourse particle.

panel.q: A friend says Да ладно! after your news. What does it express?
panel.why: Да ладно can mean "no way" in a friendly tone.

teach.model: Use connectors: кстати for a related new point, на самом деле to correct, вот именно to confirm. Disagree gently with Я не совсем согласен. Ask politely with Не могли бы вы...?

trip.prompt: Read a short dialogue and circle the connecting words.

stages.title: Formal and informal registers
stages.hook: You greet your friend with "Привет" and your teacher with "Здравствуйте". What else changes with register?
explain: Register means the level of formality. The informal ты and the formal вы affect the verb: Дай мне ручку (informal) and Дайте мне ручку (formal). Informal Извини becomes Извините. Goodbye can be Пока (casual) or Всего доброго (formal).

At school or work address older people by first name and patronymic: Иван Петрович. In an e-mail start with Добрый день, ... or Уважаемый ... A phrase like Не подскажете, который час? (Could you tell me what time it is?) is polite in the street.
stages.mnemonic: Ты is the handshake, вы is the bow.
sentences: Could you tell me what time it is?

gq.q: How do you address an older teacher called Ольга Ивановна?
gq.why: First name and patronymic plus вы is respectful.
The -те ending is the formal or plural imperative.

panel.q: Why does the imperative change between Дай and Дайте?
o: The ending -те marks plural or polite address
panel.why: Register affects verb forms.

panel.q: A new classmate of your age uses ты. What does it show?
panel.why: Ты is normal among peers.

panel.q: Which e-mail opening is appropriate for an unknown professor?
panel.why: Formal register needs вы or name and patronymic.

teach.model: Russian marks formality with ты and вы. The imperative changes: Дай for a friend and Дайте for polite use. Use first name and patronymic for older people.

points.ask: How do I address a teacher?

trip.prompt: Read about how languages show politeness and note the Russian example.

stages.title: Reading articles and literature
stages.hook: Which Russian poet is often called the founder of modern Russian literature?
explain: Alexander Pushkin (1799–1837) wrote Евгений Онегин, a novel in verse, and shaped the modern literary language. Lev Tolstoy wrote Война и мир and Анна Каренина, Fyodor Dostoevsky wrote Преступление и наказание, and Anton Chekhov wrote short stories and plays such as Вишнёвый сад.

To read literature, learn the words for genres: рассказ (short story), роман (novel), стихотворение (poem), and the vocabulary of analysis: сюжет (plot), тема (theme), герой (character). Newspaper articles in Russian often use the present tense for a past event in headlines.
stages.mnemonic: Pushkin writes poems, Tolstoy writes big novels, Chekhov writes short stories.
sentences: Pushkin is a great Russian poet.
This is a story about friendship.
The main character looks for his place.

gq.q: Who wrote the novel in verse Евгений Онегин?
Which genre is Вишнёвый сад by Chekhov?
gq.why: The Cherry Orchard is a play.

panel.q: Why is Pushkin called the founder of modern literary Russian?
o: He joined everyday speech and older literary language into a model style
panel.why: His works set a pattern for later writers.

panel.q: What is the difference between сюжет and тема?
o: Сюжет is the sequence of events and тема is the main idea
panel.why: Plot tells what happens; theme tells what it is about.

panel.q: Why does a headline say "Президент подписывает закон" about a past event?
o: The event is in the future
Russian headlines often use the present to sound immediate
panel.why: The historical present is common in headlines.

teach.model: Pushkin is the founder of modern literary Russian. Tolstoy, Dostoevsky and Chekhov are other great writers. Analyse a text by its plot (сюжет), theme (тема) and character (герой).

trip.prompt: Read the first section and note two works with their genres.

stages.title: Essay and correspondence writing
stages.hook: In a polite letter to one person, Russians write the word "Вы" with a capital letter. Why?
explain: An essay has three parts: introduction (введение), main part (основная часть) and conclusion (заключение). Link ideas with во-первых... во-вторых..., таким образом (thus), итак (so) and в заключение (in conclusion).

A formal letter begins Уважаемый господин Иванов, and ends С уважением, followed by the name. In a letter to one person the polite Вы and Ваш are capitalised. Use Прошу вас to ask, and Прилагаю to say that something is attached.
stages.mnemonic: Введение opens, основная часть builds, заключение closes.
sentences: Please reply as soon as possible.
In conclusion I want to say thank you.

gq.q: How do you end a formal letter?
In a personal letter to one person, how is the polite "you" written?
gq.why: The capital Вы shows personal respect in a letter.

panel.q: Which order is typical for an essay?
panel.why: The three-part structure guides the reader.

panel.q: Why use Таким образом in the last paragraph?
o: It signals a summary of what has been shown
panel.why: It means "thus" and introduces a conclusion.

panel.q: Which opening is right for a letter to a company director?
panel.why: Respectful forms with name and patronymic are polite.

teach.topic: Writing letters and essays in Russian
teach.model: An essay has a введение, основная часть and заключение. Use linking words like во-первых, во-вторых and таким образом. A formal letter starts Уважаемый... and ends С уважением.

points.ask: How do I start and end a letter?

trip.prompt: Look at a model formal letter and mark the greeting and closing.

stages.title: Translation fundamentals
stages.hook: If you translate "I miss you" word by word into Russian, you may say something strange. Why?
explain: Good translation carries meaning, not just words. A literal translation (дословный перевод) often fails. "I miss you" is Я скучаю по тебе, with по and the dative. Russian У меня есть кот is the usual way to say "I have a cat".

Translators watch for false friends, context and register, and use a dictionary and a bilingual sense of style. Russian has no articles, so a translator into English must decide between "a" and "the" by context. The aspects of Russian verbs, perfective and imperfective, often need extra words in English.
stages.mnemonic: Translate the message, not the words.
sentences: A literal translation is not always accurate.
You need to understand the meaning of the sentence.

gq.q: How do you say "I miss you" naturally?
gq.why: Скучать по plus the dative is the natural construction.

gq.q: Why can a literal translation be wrong?
o: Languages express ideas with different structures
gq.why: Structures and idioms differ between languages.

panel.q: Translating from Russian into English, how do you decide between "a" and "the"?
o: From context, since Russian has no articles
panel.why: The translator reads context to choose.

panel.q: Why is магазин → "magazine" a mistake?
o: It is a false friend: магазин means shop
panel.why: False friends look the same but differ in meaning.

panel.q: Which approach is better for a proverb?
o: Find an equivalent proverb in the target language
panel.why: A proverb is best matched by a similar saying.

teach.model: Good translation transfers meaning, not just words. Watch for false friends, context and register. Russian has no articles, so you must choose a or the from context.

trip.prompt: Read about equivalence in translation and note one example.

stages.title: Regional varieties and cultural context
stages.hook: Russia spans 11 time zones. Do all Russians speak and live in the same way?
explain: Russian is spoken across a huge area and in many countries as a first or second language. The standard literary language is based on the speech of Moscow, but regional speech differs. In many southern and Moscow varieties unstressed о sounds like a ("akanye"), while some northern dialects keep a clear о ("okanye").

Culture shapes everyday life. A дача is a country house for summer weekends, a самовар is a tea urn, and Масленица is a spring festival with pancakes (блины) before Orthodox Lent. Russians celebrate Новый год with a decorated tree and Дед Мороз, and Orthodox Christmas is on 7 January.
stages.mnemonic: Moscow says "malako", the north may say "moloko".
sentences: In summer we live at the dacha.

gq.why: It is a festival before Lent.
Akanye is common in standard Russian.

panel.q: Why does Russia have regional dialect differences?
o: Because the language spread over a large area over centuries
Because all Russians live in cities
panel.why: Geography and history shape variation.

panel.q: Why is Russian also used outside Russia?
o: It is the only language there
It is a first or second language in many neighbouring countries
panel.why: Many people in former Soviet countries use Russian.

panel.q: Why is Orthodox Christmas on 7 January?
o: The Russian Orthodox Church follows the Julian calendar
It is a school holiday only
panel.why: Julian dates are about 13 days later than Gregorian ones.

teach.model: Standard Russian is based on Moscow speech, but regions differ: akanye in the south and okanye in the north. Culture includes дача, самовар, Масленица and Новый год. Orthodox Christmas is on 7 January.

trip.prompt: Read about the festival and note two traditions.

stages.title: Structured debates and presentations
stages.hook: You must convince a classroom in two minutes. How do you start and organise your argument in Russian?
explain: A presentation begins with a greeting and the topic: Добрый день, уважаемые слушатели! Сегодня я расскажу о... A debate uses thesis (тезис), argument (аргумент), example (пример) and conclusion (вывод). Introduce your view: По моему мнению...

To contrast ideas, use С одной стороны... с другой стороны... To object politely say Позвольте возразить (Allow me to object). To end, summarise: Из этого следует вывод... and thank the audience: Спасибо за внимание!
stages.mnemonic: Тезис, аргумент, пример, вывод: four steps to persuade.
sentences: In my opinion, this is important.
I want to give an example.

gq.q: How do you thank the audience at the end?
gq.why: It is the usual closing of a presentation.

panel.q: Why does a speaker give an example after an argument?
o: Examples make an abstract claim concrete and believable
panel.why: Evidence supports the claim.

panel.q: Which is a polite way to disagree in a debate?
panel.why: Позвольте возразить keeps respect.

panel.q: What does "с одной стороны... с другой стороны" do?
o: It balances two points of view
panel.why: It presents two sides of an issue.

teach.model: Start with a greeting and topic. State a thesis, give arguments and examples, and end with a conclusion. Disagree politely with Позвольте возразить and thank the audience.

points.ask: How do I organise a talk?

trip.prompt: Watch or read a short debate and list one argument and one example.
